correctness.rationale: All integer lengths are covered by the three disjoint ranges for powers of three plus n=1. The Cantor one-position gap identity \(1+3^{\nu_2(j)}\) yields the required palindrome-prefix obstruction, rigorously ruling out cross-block duplicates at length \(m+1\). Two marker/one-location arguments prove distinctness of all shorter-start windows at lengths \(2m+1\) and \(3m\), without assumptions stronger than those stated. Explicit identical-factor witnesses give the reverse inequalities. Literal independent direct enumeration matched the formula at all 729 initial lengths; the proof, not that finite scan, establishes the infinite statement.

value.rationale: This classifies a natural order-sensitive word-complexity invariant for every factor length of a canonical non-uniformly recurrent automatic sequence. Three genuinely different first-repeat mechanisms (repeated blocks, adjacent windows in a long zero gap, and shifted long prefix) create exact ternary staircase jumps; the full result is not obtainable from ordinary Cantor factor complexity. It adds a concrete all-length benchmark next to the 2015 exact results for the Thue–Morse, Fibonacci and Tribonacci families.
